WATER: Make a 'W' hand with your dominant hand (three middle fingers up, thumb and pinky tucked). Tap the tip of your index finger on your chin a couple of times, like touching a drop of water to your mouth.
EAT: Bring the tips of your fingers and thumb together on your dominant hand (like holding a small bite of food) and tap them to your lips a few times, as if you're eating.
DRINK: Shape your dominant hand like you're holding a cup, then tilt your hand toward your mouth as if taking a sip from a glass.
HOME: Make a flat 'O' hand (fingertips touching thumb). Touch your cheek near the corner of your mouth, then move back and slightly up to touch near your ear, like showing where you live and sleep.
SLEEP: Hold an open hand in front of your face, palm toward you. Slowly pull your hand down while letting the fingers and thumb come together, as your eyes 'close,' like drifting off to sleep.
WHERE: Hold up your dominant index finger in front of you, palm facing out. Gently wiggle it side to side with your eyebrows lowered, like asking, 'Where?'
WHO: Make an 'L' handshape, place the thumb near your chin, and gently bend or wiggle the index finger while your lips are slightly pursed, as if asking, 'Who is it?'
WHY: Touch your fingertips to the side of your forehead, then move your hand out and down, changing into a 'Y' handshape (thumb and pinky out), like a thought turning into a 'why?' question.
YES: Make an 'S' hand (a fist) and move it up and down at the wrist, like your fist is nodding its head 'yes.'
NO: Hold up your hand with index and middle fingers together and thumb open. Tap the two fingers to the thumb a couple of times, like a mouth closing to say 'no.'
HELLO: Place your flat dominant hand at your forehead, like a salute, then move it outward in a small arc to send a friendly 'hello.'
GOODBYE: Raise your dominant hand, palm facing out, and open and close your fingers a few times in a relaxed wave to say 'goodbye.'
PLEASE: Place your flat palm on the center of your chest and move it in a small circle, showing polite feeling from the heart.
THANK YOU: Touch the fingertips of your dominant hand to your chin or lips, then move your hand forward and slightly down away from your face, like you're sending a 'thank you' out to someone.
SORRY: Make an 'S' hand (fist), place it on the center of your chest, and rub it in small circles with an apologetic face.
OK: Most often, signers simply fingerspell O-K with the dominant hand, palm facing out, as a quick way to show 'okay,' 'alright,' or agreement.
NOW: Make 'Y' handshapes with both hands (thumb and pinky out). Hold them in front of you, palms up, then drop them slightly down at the same time, like showing something is happening right now.
NICE: Hold your non-dominant hand palm up. With your dominant hand flat, palm down, slide it smoothly across the other hand from heel to fingertips, like smoothing something clean and nice.
LIKE: Place your dominant open hand on your chest, then pull it slightly away while bringing your thumb and middle finger together, as if you're gently pulling a feeling of 'like' out of your chest.
DON'T LIKE: Start like LIKE: open hand on your chest, then pull it away bringing thumb and middle finger together. As your hand moves away, flick your fingers open and slightly down with a 'yuck' face, like tossing something you don't like.
HUNGRY: Make a 'C' handshape and place it at the top of your chest. Move it straight down the center of your torso, like food traveling down an empty stomach.
HOT: Shape your dominant hand like a loose claw near your open mouth, then quickly turn the hand outward and away, as if letting hot air or hot food out.
CLEAN: Hold your non-dominant hand palm up. With your dominant hand flat, palm down, brush across the upturned palm several times, like wiping a surface clean.
DIRTY: Place the back of your relaxed dominant hand under your chin, palm down, and wiggle your fingers loosely with a slightly scrunched expression, like something feels dirty or messy.
PAY: Hold your non-dominant hand flat, palm up. Touch the tip of your dominant index or middle finger to the palm, then flick it forward, like sliding money toward someone to pay.
PHONE: Make a 'Y' handshape (thumb and pinky out). Place your thumb near your ear and your pinky near your mouth, like holding a phone to talk.
WAIT: Hold both hands in front of you, palms up, fingers relaxed and slightly spread. Gently wiggle your fingers and move your hands a little back and forth, like telling someone to 'hang on, wait.'
LATER: Hold your non-dominant hand upright, palm facing in like a wall. Make an 'L' with your dominant hand, thumb touching the non-dominant palm. Rotate the 'L' forward, like pointing to a time later on.
AGAIN: Hold your non-dominant hand flat, palm up. With your dominant hand slightly cupped, fingertips together, bring your fingertips down into the center of the non-dominant palm, like asking to do something 'again.'
COOL: Hold both hands open with fingers spread near your face, palms toward you. Wiggle or flap your fingers back toward your face a couple of times, as if you feel a cool breeze on your skin.
BUSY: Rest your non-dominant hand in front of you (often as a fist). Place the bottom edge of your dominant flat hand on the back or wrist of the non-dominant hand and move it side to side or in quick small motions, like everything is moving and busy.
READY: Make 'R' handshapes with both hands. Hold them in front of you side by side, then move them outward apart in a smooth motion, like opening double doors to show you're ready.
EXCUSE-ME: Hold your non-dominant hand flat, palm up. With your dominant hand slightly bent at the knuckles, brush your fingertips across the non-dominant palm a couple of times, with a polite expression, like saying 'excuse me' or 'pardon me.'
SEE-YOU: Make a 'V' handshape with your dominant hand, palm in. Touch the middle finger near your eye for SEE, then move the 'V' outward toward the person, like your eyes are going with them: 'see you.'
BATHROOM: Make a 'T' handshape (thumb between index and middle fingers) with your dominant hand and shake it side to side near your shoulder, like asking, 'Where's the bathroom?'
HAPPY: Place one or both open hands on your upper chest, palms in. Move them upward in small circles or strokes with a smiling face, like happy feelings rising up.
SAD: Hold both hands open in front of your face, palms toward you, fingers relaxed. Move your hands downward along your face with a sad expression, like your feelings are sliding down.
TIRED: Place the fingertips of both hands on your upper chest, palms in. Let your elbows drop and your shoulders slump forward, showing your body sinking with tiredness.
SICK: Touch the middle finger of one hand to your forehead and the middle finger of the other hand to your chest, palms in, with a strained expression, as if you feel sick in both head and body.
FAMILY: Make 'F' handshapes with both hands (thumb and index touching in a circle). Touch the circles together in front of you, then move them outward in a small circle and back together, like drawing a circle of family around you.
FRIEND: Extend the index fingers of both hands. Hook one index finger over the other, then switch and hook them the opposite way, like two people linking arms as friends.
HELP: Hold your non-dominant hand palm up like a platform. Make an 'A' handshape (thumb up) with your dominant hand and place the fist on that palm, then lift both hands upward together, like helping someone up.
WANT: Hold both hands out in front of you, palms up, fingers relaxed and slightly curved. Pull your hands toward your body while curling the fingers a bit more, like drawing what you want toward yourself.
SCHOOL: Hold both hands flat with palms facing each other. Clap the dominant hand down onto the non-dominant hand twice, like two flat books coming together for school.
WORK: Make 'S' handshapes (fists) with both hands. Hold the non-dominant fist in front of you, palm down, and tap the wrist or back of it with the bottom of your dominant fist a couple of times, like tools hitting at work.
LOVE: Cross both arms over your chest with fists closed, as if giving yourself a big hug, showing love and affection.
FINISH: Hold both hands in front of you, palms facing in, fingers spread. Twist your wrists so your palms turn outward with a quick motion and 'done' face, like saying 'finished / all done.'
TIME: Hold your non-dominant hand in a relaxed fist with the back facing up, like wearing a watch. Tap the top of that wrist with the tip of your dominant index finger, as if pointing at the time on a watch.
GO: Point forward with your index finger on one or both hands. Start closer to your body, then move your hands outward in the direction of travel, like telling someone to go.
COME: Point with your index finger on one or both hands, starting farther out in front of you and then pulling your hands toward your body, like inviting someone to come closer.
